subject: Post-demo: data sharing & telemetry vendor evaluation — proposed actions
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finsystems.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T14:02:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: data sharing & telemetry vendor evaluation — proposed actions

Hi Aisha — great to meet today, thanks for the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Data surface: You confirmed logs + anonymized telemetry from inference calls (model_id, latency, SDK version, request metadata) are acceptable to evaluate throughput. PII and raw customer prompts are NOT to be exported to any telemetry vendor.
2) Retention: FinSystems prefers telemetry retained no more than 90 days for analytics; you may require a 12-month retention for auditable logs in a separate retention bucket — flagged as a conditional requirement.
3) Subprocessors: you asked for the list of telemetry & infra subprocessors used by Redwood for hosted and marketplace flows.

Proposed actions:
- I attached our SOC 2 snapshot and a simplified dataflow diagram (see attachments). Neha will confirm encryption-at-rest and access control specifics for telemetry buckets.
- Share redacted telemetry fields schema we propose for FinSystems (no prompt content).
- If acceptable, we’ll produce a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for a pilot (test tenancy, retention config, telemetry scope).

Can you confirm 1) the 90-day default is acceptable for analytics pipelines and 2) whether you need a separate 12-month audit bucket for specific logs? Happy to jump on a 20m follow-up if you prefer.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: SOC2_Type_2_Redwood_2026.pdf (pdf), redwood-dataflow-telemetry.png (image), proposed-map-v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finsystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: PlatformOps Team <platformops@finsystems.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data sharing & telemetry vendor evaluation — proposed actions

Thanks Sean — helpful recap. Quick answers from our side: 
- 90 days for analytics pipeline is fine as a baseline.
- We do need a separate 12-month retention for audit logs tied to production incidents (security/ops review). Those logs can be more restricted in scope.
- Telemetry vendor constraint: we use Telemetrix for platform metrics and prefer vendor access to be limited to aggregated/hashed data only. No raw prompts or customer identifiers.

Can Neha confirm whether Redwood can route telemetry to a customer-managed storage location (S3) for the 12-month audit bucket? If not, what alternate controls can you offer (e.g., customer-specific encryption keys, limited RBAC)?

Also, please add proposed MAP milestones (pilot start, test dataset, retention config) to the drive link you mentioned.

—Aisha
Aisha Khan
Director, Platform Operations | FinSystems
aisha.khan@finsystems.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finsystems.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data sharing & telemetry vendor evaluation — proposed actions

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clarity. Answers below and controls we can offer: 

- Customer-managed audit bucket: yes — for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers we support routing telemetry to a customer-owned S3/GCS with your KMS. For hosted customers we can also configure a customer-scoped storage location (SSE-C or customer-managed KMS) as part of the pilot; we’ll need an onboarding ticket for infra ops. 

- Access & encryption: telemetry in analytics pipelines is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.3). RBAC: telemetry access is limited to a small ops role and is logged. We can provide a short role/permission matrix and an IAM policy snippet.

- Subprocessors & vendor access: Telemetry third-parties (metrics, alerting) only receive aggregated metrics and hashed identifiers. We will not send raw prompts or PII. I attached a redwood-dataflow diagram and a SOC2 summary for your security team to review.

Next steps I’ll take: 
1) Provide a redacted telemetry schema (fields that will be exported) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Draft MAP milestones in the Drive folder (pilot kick, retention config, go/no-go) and share an editable copy.
3) If Telemetrix requires vendor access, we’ll list the exact fields and the transformation (hashing/aggregation) performed before export.

If helpful, Marissa can coordinate a short legal touchpoint on subprocessors and any DPA redlines.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-telemetry.png, SOC2_Type_2_Redwood_2026.pdf

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finsystems.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: PlatformOps Team <platformops@finsystems.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data sharing & telemetry vendor evaluation — proposed actions

Hi Neha/Sean — this looks good and addresses our main blockers. Two quick asks before we start the pilot:

1) Please confirm the exact fields you’ll export to Telemetrix and the hashing algorithm used (sha256 ok).
2) Add a note in the MAP that the 12-month bucket will be customer-managed with our KMS; if Redwood hosts it, we need dedicated CMKs and a view-only audit role for FinSystems.

If you can drop the schema and MAP draft in the Drive folder today we’ll route to legal and infra for signoff. Thanks — will aim to confirm pilot start next week.

Regards,
Aisha
